artworks.title: American Snipe
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts three snipe birds in a natural setting. The birds are shown in detail interacting with each other. One bird is slightly larger than the others and is standing among reeds. The background shows a calm body of water reflecting the sky, with trees and a house in the distance. The color palette is Earthy with browns and greens for the birds and vegetation, while the water and sky are in muted blues and grays.

artworks.title: Common Gallinule
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird standing near a body of water. The image portrays a bird with a dark body and distinctive bright red beak and frontal shield, walking on long greenish legs with large feet. It is depicted with one foot forward, positioned on a grassy patch near some water. The background shows a body of water with some rocks and reeds along the shoreline. The detail and style suggest a focus on ornithological accuracy. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Uria Brunnichii
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is an image of a bird in flight over water. The bird has dark feathers on its back and wings, and white feathers underneath. It has a black beak, red eyes, and webbed feet. The background shows a gradient from light to dark, resembling a sky, with waves in the water below. The painting is detailed, focusing on the bird's feathers. It is reminiscent of the style of John James Audubon, known for detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Eider Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of eider ducks in a natural setting. The image features three ducks amid lush grasses. The ducks’ feathers are rendered in detailed, natural colors, with notable variations in pattern across the different birds. The background is a mix of sky and dense foliage.

artworks.title: Velvet Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two ducks on a rocky shore. One duck is resting and the other is standing. The duck on the left has brown feathers with white patches on its face and sides, pink legs, and webbed feet. The duck on the right has a dark body, a white patch near its wings, and an orange bill. Both ducks are on rocks with a hint of water in the background. The painting showcases detailed textures and precision in the ducks' anatomy, following the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Razor Bill
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting featuring two razorbill birds floating on the water near a rocky coastline. The painting depicts two birds with black feathers on their heads, backs, and tails, and white underbellies. One bird has its beak open, displaying its bright yellow interior, while the other bird appears calm. The setting includes a body of teal water with gentle waves, and in the background, there is a jagged rocky landscape under a pale sky. The text at the bottom of the painting indicates the artist's name, as well as the bird species' name. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Puffin
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two puffins in a coastal setting. The scene features one puffin standing on a rocky outcrop while another peeks out from a burrow nestled in grassy terrain. The puffin standing outside showcases its colorful beak and red feet, along with its black and white plumage. The background includes a body of water leading to distant landforms under a pale sky. This illustration is detailed and scientific.

artworks.title: Common Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two gulls, one with lighter plumage and the other with a mottled brown and white pattern. The color palette includes grays, browns, and white, with hints of yellow and pink. The light-colored gull is on the left, facing upward and slightly to the right, while the brown gull is on the right, facing the viewer. In the foreground, there are multicolored shells on the ground.

artworks.title: American Pied-Bill Dobchick
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two American Pied-bill Dobchicks swimming in a body of water surrounded by lush greenery. The painting depicts two birds swimming closely together, their sleek brown and white bodies partially submerged in the water. They have sharp beaks and are positioned in a dynamic diagonal that guides the viewer's eye from the foreground to the background, through a lush array of green, leaf-filled plants. The background is rich with dense vegetation, featuring long, elegant reeds and a small branch with a slightly twisted form adding variety to the scene.

artworks.title: Tufted Auk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The painting depicts two tufted auks among rocks and grass. One bird is standing on the right, while the other is seated on the left. The birds display yellow and red beaks, with dark plumage and lighter feathers on the head. The seated bird is shown in a resting posture. Grasses are seen throughout the scene, and the background complements the birds' features. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Arctic Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print showing a bird diving towards water with its wings and tail spread out. The bird has a thin pink beak and pink feet, a black patch on the top of its head, a white throat and tail, and a gray body and wings. The background shows a gray-blue sky with heavy clouds and a blue, slightly wavy ocean below. The print is surrounded by a border of off-white paper, and there are some lines of text below it.

artworks.title: Brown Pelican
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James

artworks.title: Florida Cormorant
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a cormorant perched on a branch by the water. The cormorant is detailed with an elongated neck, sharp beak, and green plumage with orange accents. It is gripping the branch with its talons. In the background, there are trees, a pastel sky, and more cormorants on the water. The painting captures the serenity of the cormorant's habitat.

artworks.title: Jager
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a large bird standing on a grassy hillock by the sea. The bird has a broad chest with dark brown feathers forming a pattern, and its wings are rich deep brown, contrasting with the lighter shades of its chest and neck. Its head is detailed, with a dark cap, and its beak has a sharp hook at the end. It is perched solidly on the ground, with webbed feet firmly planted, next to a large, open seashell. The background shows silhouettes of distant icebergs against a pale sky and calm sea.

artworks.title: Wilson's Phalarope
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds by a water's edge. One bird is standing on the ground surrounded by greenery, while the other is depicted in flight above. The grounded bird is on a small patch of earth with rocks and grass, looking towards the water. The flying bird has its wings fully extended, showcasing patterns in its feathers. The surroundings include the water's edge and grass, creating a natural habitat. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Red Phalarope
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three phalaropes in different poses. The image shows one phalarope in flight, one standing on rocky ground, and another perched on a rock. Each bird has detailed plumage in earthy tones of brown, reds, grays, and blacks. The background includes a sky and a distant seascape, with grassy elements in the foreground. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Purple Heron
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two herons standing amidst vegetation. The herons have intricate details in their plumage and are surrounded by green leaves and grasses. In the background, there is a mountain and cloudy sky. The style is similar to that of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Double-crested Cormorant
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Double-crested Cormorant perched on a rock. The artwork depicts a large bird with dark plumage and distinctive feather crests on its head, set against a coastal background with cliffs and water. The cormorant is positioned with its body facing slightly away but its head turned, showcasing its long, hooked beak. Its detailed feathers are intricately painted, emphasizing their texture and form. In the distance, other birds can be faintly seen along the shore. The background is composed of soft blues and grays, creating a serene marine scene. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Hudsonian Godwit
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two Hudsonian Godwits. The bird on the left has its wings slightly spread out, while the bird on the right is standing upright. The color palette includes browns, grays, muted reds, with highlights of white and black on the wings. The bird on the left is lying down with its wings raised, angled diagonally across the bottom left corner of the image. The bird on the right is standing, facing left with legs firmly on the ground.

artworks.title: Horned Grebe
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Horned Grebes beside water and grass. One bird is in breeding plumage with vibrant red and brown colors, a green-black neck, and an orange and black crest. The other bird, likely the female in winter plumage, has a black and white color palette. Both birds are depicted in a detailed and realistic style against a background of green grass and water. This painting is reminiscent of John James Audubon's work.

artworks.title: Fork-tailed Petrel
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two fork-tail petrels flying over stormy ocean waves. The painting illustrates two birds with distinct forked tails and mostly dark plumage. They are depicted with outstretched wings, gliding above rolling waves. The sky is painted to appear overcast and ominous, with layered shades of gray clouds. The dynamic poses of the birds and the turbulent sea below create a sense of motion and energy in the scene.

artworks.title: Hooping Crane
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a large bird standing near a body of water with more birds in the background. The painting depicts a detailed representation of the bird standing on grass near a body of water. The bird has a gray body, long legs, an extended neck, and a red patch on its head. The background features a landscape with a blue water body, and more birds are visible in the distance against a backdrop of hills or mountains.

artworks.title: Tropic Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two white and black birds with long tails near a body of water. The full description of the image shows one bird perched on a rock, and another in mid-flight, with both birds exhibiting long, elegant tail feathers. The bird on the rock is facing slightly to the right, with bright yellow feet visible, and an ocean with gentle waves extends across the background under a moody sky filled with dark clouds. The detailed brushwork highlights the textures of the birds' feathers, the rock's surface, and the subtle undulations of the water. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Pigmy Curlew
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two birds near water. The description includes two wading birds with long legs and beaks, on a rocky bank by water. One bird has a brown and white body and a long, curved beak. The other bird has striking reddish plumage and wing patterns. There is lush green grass surrounding them, hinting at a marshy habitat.
